source_text:
Μὴ οὐ δύναμαι ὑμῖν τὰ ἐπουράνια γράψαι; ἀλλὰ φοβοῦμαι, μὴ νηπίοις οὖσιν ὑμῖν βλάβην παραθῶ: καὶ συγγνωμονεῖτέ μοι, μήποτε οὐ δυνηθέντες χωρῆσαι στραγγαλωθῆτε.
καὶ γὰρ ἐγώ, οὐ καθότι δέδεμαι καὶ δύναμαι νοεῖν τὰ ἐπουράνια καὶ τὰς τοποθεσίας τὰς ἀγγελικὰς καὶ τὰς συστάσεις τὰς ἀρχοντικάς, ὁρατά τε καὶ ἀόρατα, παρὰ τοῦτο ἤδη καὶ μαθητής εἰμι. πολλὰ γὰρ ἡμῖν λείπει, ἵνα θεοῦ μὴ λειπώμεθα.
thought_title: Heavenly knowledge and the limits of discipleship
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the church in Tralles, explaining why he withholds deeper heavenly teaching from them and reflecting on his own unworthiness as a disciple.
pass_a_gloss: Am I not able to write to you the heavenly things? But I am afraid, lest, since you are infants, I set before you harm: and pardon me, lest, not being able to contain it, you be strangled. For I too, not because I am bound and am able to understand the heavenly things and the angelic positions and the assemblies of the rulers, visible and invisible, am I already also a disciple on account of this. For many things are lacking to us, so that we may not be lacking of God.

choices.why: Keeps the neuter plural substantive force of the Greek, referring to heavenly realities or teachings as a class.
Renders the causal participle with the dative of possession, preserving the reason for Ignatius's fear.
Keeps the metaphor of placing food before someone, matching the following image of being strangled by what cannot be contained.
Preserves the vivid physical image of choking on food one cannot swallow, which fits the feeding metaphor.
Renders τοποθεσία literally as 'positions' to keep the spatial and hierarchical sense of angelic orders.
Keeps σύστασις as 'assemblies' and ἀρχοντικός as 'of the rulers,' preserving the cosmic hierarchy of visible and invisible powers.

pass_b_english: Can I not write to you about heavenly things? I am afraid to, because you are still infants. I fear I would set before you something harmful. Forgive me: perhaps you could not take it in, and you would choke on it.

For even I, though I am in chains and can understand heavenly things, the ranks of the angels and the assemblies of the rulers, visible and invisible, am not yet a disciple for that reason. For we still lack much if we are not to fall short of God.

problems.quote: not because I am bound and can understand the heavenly things, the angelic positions, and the assemblies of the rulers, visible and invisible, am I already a disciple because of this
problems.source_quote: οὐ καθότι δέδεμαι καὶ δύναμαι νοεῖν τὰ ἐπουράνια καὶ τὰς τοποθεσίας τὰς ἀγγελικὰς καὶ τὰς συστάσεις τὰς ἀρχοντικάς, ὁρατά τε καὶ ἀόρατα, παρὰ τοῦτο ἤδη καὶ μαθητής εἰμι
problems.why: Source says 'not because I am bound and can understand... am I already a disciple.' English inserts 'because of this,' implying being bound/understanding makes him a disciple.
problems.fix: For even I, not because I am bound and can understand the heavenly things, the angelic positions, and the assemblies of the rulers, visible and invisible, am I already a disciple.
problems.ruling: Greek 'οὐ καθότι ... παρὰ τοῦτο' means 'not because ... apart from this', but English adds 'because of this', reversing causality.

edits.old: For even I, not because I am bound and can understand the heavenly things, the angelic positions, and the assemblies of the rulers, visible and invisible, am I already a disciple because of this.
edits.new: For even I, not because I am bound and can understand the heavenly things, the angelic positions, and the assemblies of the rulers, visible and invisible, am I already a disciple.

fixed: Removed 'because of this' from the English, which incorrectly implied that being bound and understanding made him a disciple; the source says he is not already a disciple on account of these things.

problems.source_quote: παρὰ τοῦτο ἤδη καὶ μαθητής εἰμι
problems.why: παρὰ τοῦτο means 'besides this' or 'beyond this,' not 'because of this.' The sense flips: Ignatius says he is a disciple despite/besides these things, not because of them.
problems.fix: besides this, I am even now a disciple
problems.ruling: παρὰ τοῦτο ἤδη καὶ μαθητής εἰμι means 'apart from this I am already a disciple', not 'because of this', and English mis‑renders as a question.

problems.quote: if you cannot contain it, you may be strangled.
problems.why: Greek says ‘lest, being unable to endure, you be strangled’; English changes ‘endure’ to ‘contain’ and replaces ‘lest’ with a simple conditional, altering meaning.
problems.fix: And be indulgent with me, lest, being unable to endure, you are strangled.
problems.ruling: χωρῆσαι means 'endure/contain'; μήποτε='lest' not 'if'; conditional replaces purpose clause, changing meaning.

edits.old: And pardon me: if you cannot contain it, you may be strangled.
edits.new: And pardon me, lest, being unable to endure it, you be strangled.
besides this, I am even now a disciple.

problems.quote: For much is lacking to us, so that we may not be lacking from God
problems.why: Paradoxical: lacking so as not to lack; wordplay on 'lacking' obscured.
problems.fix: Clarify wordplay: 'We still lack much, so that we may not be found lacking by God.'

edits.old: For much is lacking to us, so that we may not be lacking from God.
edits.new: We still lack much, so that we may not be found lacking by God.

fixed: The wordplay on 'lacking' was obscured; clarified as 'We still lack much, so that we may not be found lacking by God.'

problems.quote: Pardon me, lest you be unable to endure it and be strangled.
problems.why: Mixed metaphor: 'strangled' as figurative for choking on advanced teaching is abrupt and violent.
problems.fix: Consider 'choked' or note metaphor of premature weaning/feeding.

edits.old: Pardon me, lest you be unable to endure it and be strangled.
edits.new: Pardon me, lest you be unable to endure it and be choked.

problems.quote: We still lack much, so that we may not be found lacking by God.
problems.why: Circular: lack much to not be found lacking.
problems.fix: Clarify: 'we still need much growth, lest we be found wanting.'

edits.old: We still lack much, so that we may not be found lacking by God.
edits.new: We still lack much, so that we may not be lacking in God.

fixed: The source reads πολλὰ γὰρ ἡμῖν λείπει, ἵνα θεοῦ μὴ λειπώμεθα, literally 'for many things are lacking to us, so that we may not be lacking of God.' The English 'found lacking by God' misstates the genitive θεοῦ as an agent, but it is the object of lacking. The suggested 'need much growth' is too free. Changed to 'lacking in God' to preserve the genitive object while keeping the sentence natural.

last_rejected.quote: not because I am bound and can understand the heavenly things, the angelic positions, and the assemblies of the rulers, visible and invisible, besides this, I am even now a disciple
last_rejected.source_quote: οὐ καθότι δέδεμαι καὶ δύναμαι νοεῖν τὰ ἐπουράνια καὶ τὰς τοποθεσίας τὰς ἀγγελικὰς καὶ τὰς συστάσεις τὰς ἀρχοντικάς, ὁρατά τε καὶ ἀόρατα, παρὰ τοῦτο ἤδη καὶ μαθητής εἰμι
last_rejected.why: παρὰ τοῦτο means 'despite this' or 'beyond this,' not 'besides this'; the sense is: despite all this knowledge, I am still a disciple.
last_rejected.fix: despite this I am even now a disciple
last_rejected.ruling: παρὰ τοῦτο means 'apart from' or 'besides', translation 'besides this' is acceptable, not a major error.

polish.changed: Clarified the incomplete sentence by supplying the implied main clause 'am not yet a disciple on that account,' and smoothed the syntax for modern readers while preserving every claim and qualification.

notes.quote: For even I, not because I am bound and can understand the heavenly things
notes.why: The sentence breaks off and never completes its thought.
notes.fix: Supply the missing clause, e.g., 'even I am not yet able to explain them.'

polish.changed: Clarified the speaker as Ignatius, smoothed the sentence flow, and made the pronoun references explicit while preserving every claim and qualification.

notes.quote: the angelic positions, and the assemblies of the rulers
notes.why: Cosmological references to angelic hierarchies unexplained.
notes.fix: Note these refer to celestial orders, a common Jewish-Christian cosmology.

polish.changed: Clarified 'angelic positions' to 'angelic orders' for natural modern phrasing while preserving the technical celestial terminology.

notes.quote: the angelic positions, and the assemblies of the rulers, visible and invisible
notes.why: Technical celestial terminology without explanation; 'positions' and 'assemblies' are unclear.
notes.fix: Add note: 'positions' (Greek: tagmata) and 'assemblies' (synodoi) refer to angelic hierarchies.

polish.changed: I kept the original wording but clarified the logical structure of the second paragraph by repeating 'though' before the second concessive clause, so the contrast between Ignatius's knowledge and his not yet being a disciple is easier to follow.

notes.quote: For even I, though I am bound and can understand heavenly things, the angelic orders, and the assemblies of the rulers, visible and invisible, am not yet a disciple on that account.
notes.why: Clause 'can understand heavenly things' seems to claim knowledge, but 'am not yet a disciple' contradicts; logical connection garbled.
notes.fix: Clarify: 'even though I have been granted to understand... I am not thereby made a disciple.'

polish.changed: Clarified the conditional fear in the first paragraph, unpacked the circular final clause by rendering it as 'so that we may not lack God,' and kept the celestial terms as 'ranks of the angels' and 'assemblies of the rulers' for clarity.

notes.quote: We still lack much, so that we may not be found lacking by God.
notes.why: Circular: lack much to not be found lacking.
notes.fix: Clarify: 'we still need much growth, lest we be found wanting.'

notes.quote: the angelic orders, and the assemblies of the rulers
notes.why: Technical terms for celestial hierarchies; reader has no context for what these orders or assemblies are.
notes.fix: Note these are references to angelic hierarchies in contemporary Jewish/Christian cosmology.
